newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: CRICKET-GOUGH LEADS FIGHTBACK BUT ATHERTON FAILS AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GOUGH LEADS FIGHTBACK BUT ATHERTON FAILS AGAIN.

text.p: Darren Gough took four for 40 to bowl his side back into the game, but Mike Atherton failed again as England reached 17 for one at the close of the third day of the second test against Zimbabwe.
With Gough to the fore, Zimbabwe were bowled out for 215, a first innings lead of 59, much less than they had hoped for when they resumed at 93 for two.

But Atherton's nightmare run with the bat continued. He made just one before edging a catch to first slip from the pace of Heath Streak 13 balls into England's second innings. The captain has made just 34 runs in four innings in this series.
England were spared more embarrassment as they were offered the light with 11 overs left in a day lengthened by an hour after overnight rain had prevented play before lunch.
Zimbabwe's batsmen struggled as much as England had on the first day in conditions ideal for swing and seam bowling.
Only gritty opener Grant Flower (73) and all-rounder Paul Strang (47 not out) kept a revitalised England attack at bay.

But it took an inspired spell from Gough in mid-afternoon to get England on track. He had Dave Houghton caught down the leg side for 29 and trapped Andy Flower lbw for six. His best ball uprooted Guy Whittall's leg stump when he had scored only one.

Gough then picked up the key wicket of Grant Flower shortly after tea when he had his man caught at short mid-wicket. Flower's marathon vigil lasted over six hours. He hit just four fours and a six from 255 balls.
Strang took advantage of some lax bowling from the rest of the England attack to ensure a respectable first innings lead making his runs from just 82 balls, a remarkable rate on this slow pitch.
With more weather interruptions predicted a draw is the likely conclusion to a match where England have been second best for most of the first three days.
